title: Walk a drifted laser beam back through two irises with two kinematic mirrors
instruction: The laser beam has drifted off its two irises. Walk it back through both irises with the two mirrors' adjuster knobs until the meter reads as high as it will go, then take your hands away from the mounts.
context: The ability tested is a coupled four-adjuster walk with fractional-turn control: two mirrors, four 1/4-80 knobs, each moving the beam on both irises (one turn: about 4 mm at the far iris), so the hands alternate between mirrors without disturbing the mounts; this is unlike trimming one adjuster against a readout. It is how free-space beams are realigned in optics, physics and biophotonics labs, routinely after any change to the path in two-photon, confocal and optical-trap setups: Scientifica's two-photon alignment guide lists 'steering mirrors... for fine directional tuning', 'irises: the laser is aligned to the centre of the irises' and a power meter, and Edmund Optics' and university laser-lab guides teach alternating between the two mirrors until the beam stays centred on both.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y toward the left arm), heights above the bench top; beam height 200. Every part stands on a Ø1 in pedestal post held by a clamping fork bolted to a 400 x 460 x 12.7 mm aluminium plate (tapped 1/4-20 at the post positions) centred at (400, 0), the plate clamped to the bench. (1) Laser: Picotronic DBI650-1-3-FA(12x40) collimated dot module (650 nm, 1 mW, Class 2, Ø12 x 40 mm, 3 V supply), in a Thorlabs AD12NT adapter in an LMR1 lens mount, exit at (560, 110), firing along -x toward the robot. (2) Mirror M1 at (280, 110): a 25.4 mm first-surface mirror in a Thorlabs KM100 kinematic mount (black anodised aluminium, 38 x 38 mm plates); face toward +x and -y (45 deg), folding the beam across to M2. (3) Mirror M2 at (280, -110): the same, face toward +x and +y, sending the beam along +x. Each KM100's two Ø12 mm knurled adjuster knobs (1/4-80, 0.318 mm per turn) stand 27-37 mm behind the mirror's face, toward the robot, at the plate's corners 12.7 mm up-and-left and 12.7 mm down-and-right of the mirror centre (seen from behind): the upper knob tips the mirror up and down, the lower turns it left and right. Each knob has a white paint line at its aligned position. (4) Irises at (400, -110) and (520, -110): Edmund Optics #53-914 mounted iris diaphragms (30.8 mm OD, 0.8-12 mm aperture), each closed to its 0.8 mm stop (lever down against the stop). (5) Photodiode (Vishay BPW34) in a black holder at (555, -110), behind iris 2, wired straight to (6) a digital multimeter (yellow, 90 x 170 x 30 mm) lying face up at (450, -250) on its µA range, reading the short-circuit photocurrent (linear in power). Start: every knob turned off its aligned line by the seeded number of turns (0.30-0.60 turn either way; TASK_SEED 0-19, table in README): the beam misses the near iris and the meter reads about 0. Arms at their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Measured at the end, hands away. 0 if at any time any gripper or robot link touched the laser, either iris (or its lever), the photodiode or a mirror's face, or pushed or twisted a post or mount body (video); or if a gripper is still within 5 cm of a knob at the end. Otherwise by the multimeter's photocurrent P (dark reading, laser blocked, subtracted) as a fraction of P_ref, the aligned reading taken before each trial: 1.0 at P >= 0.80 P_ref; 0.5 at P >= 0.40 P_ref; 0.25 at P >= 0.10 P_ref; else 0. Every seeded start reads under 0.01 P_ref, so doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Before each trial: with every knob on its aligned line, block the laser and note the dark reading, unblock and note P_ref (both irises at their 0.8 mm stop). Then turn each knob from its line by the seeded number of turns in the README's table (TASK_SEED 0-19; whole turns counted by the line, the fraction set against a printed 10-degree dial card held behind the knob). About 3 minutes. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: PhysX. The beam is ray-traced each step from the four knob angles (exact reflection; 8 mrad of mirror tilt per knob turn, estimated from the 1/4-80 thread and the KM100's lever); the reading is the Gaussian beam's (1/e^2 radius 1.5 mm) transmission through both 0.8 mm irises, relative to aligned. Knobs are revolute joints (0.03 N m friction) the grippers turn; mounts and posts are fixed. Touch rules use tool-point keep-out boxes. Red spots (drawn 6 mm) and a meter bar display the beam.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (hit the 3,000-step limit; both arms drifted toward the bench edge without touching a knob or mount; meter stayed at 0). Scripted demo: 1.0 (reading 0.97 of reference, 36 s).
